notes: Paths use res:// (project) or user://. Absolute filesystem paths are rejected.
Send exactly ONE command per reply and wait for its result.
Scripts may be GDScript (.gd) or C# (.cs); the file extension picks the language.
For long scripts, put the path in JSON and the code in a ###GDSCRIPT### block (GDScript) or a ###CSHARP### block (C#).

tools.name: list_tools
tools.description: Return this command catalogue (names, parameters and descriptions). Use it when you are unsure which command or parameter exists.

tools.name: get_editor_state
tools.description: Report the connected Godot editor: project name and path, engine version, open scene, selected nodes, whether a project is playing, and the scripting capabilities (csharp = .NET build, dotnet = a .csproj/.sln exists, language/default).

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List files and folders inside the project. Filter by extension and recurse into subfolders.

extensions.description: Comma-separated extensions to keep, e.g. gd,tscn,godot

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file (scripts, scenes, project.godot, .tres). Returns numbered lines so you can target edits precisely.

tools.name: search_in_files
tools.description: Search text or a regular expression across project text files. Returns path, line number and the matching line.

regex.description: Treat query as a regular expression (default false)

include.description: Comma-separated extensions to search, e.g. gd,cs,tscn,cfg

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Create or overwrite a text file (.gd, .cs, .tscn, ...). Creates missing folders, rescans the project and can open the file in the editor. For scripts, prefer the code block instead of escaping the code in JSON: ###GDSCRIPT### for GDScript, ###CSHARP### for C#.

content.description: Full file content (omitted when a ###GDSCRIPT### or ###CSHARP### block follows)

open_in_editor.description: Open the file after writing (default false)

tools.name: write_files
tools.description: Write several text files (.gd, .cs, .tscn, .tres, ...) in one command. Each item is {path, content}. Use for scaffolding a feature in one turn.

open_in_editor.description: Open the first file after writing (default false)

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace an exact piece of text in a file (literal search, not regex). Safer than rewriting a whole script. Fails if the search text is missing or ambiguous unless all=true.

all.description: Replace every occurrence (default false = require exactly one)

tools.name: create_dir
tools.description: Create a folder (and parents) inside the project.

tools.name: delete_path
tools.description: Delete a file or folder. Folders require recursive=true. Use with care.

tools.name: rename_path
tools.description: Rename or move a file/folder inside the project.

overwrite.description: Replace the destination if it exists (default false)

tools.name: get_scene_tree
tools.description: Return the node tree of the currently edited scene as nested objects (name, type, scene-relative path, script).

tools.name: get_node_info
tools.description: Inspect one node: type, script, groups, children and editor-visible properties.

path.description: Scene-relative node path, "." for the root

tools.name: set_node_property
tools.description: Set one property on a node in the open scene (undoable). Strings such as "Vector2(32, 32)" are converted to the property's real type.

property.description: Property path, e.g. position or modulate

tools.name: add_node
tools.description: Add a new node of any engine type under a parent in the open scene (undoable), optionally with a GDScript or C# script attached.

type.description: Godot class, e.g. Sprite2D, Label, CharacterBody2D

script_path.description: Optional .gd or .cs script to attach to the new node

tools.name: attach_script
tools.description: Attach an existing GDScript (.gd) or C# (.cs) script to a node in the open scene, or detach it with script_path "" (undoable).

script_path.description: res:// path of the .gd/.cs script; empty string detaches

tools.name: remove_node
tools.description: Remove a node from the open scene (undoable). The scene root cannot be removed.

tools.name: select_nodes
tools.description: Select nodes in the editor so the human can see what you are working on.

tools.name: instantiate_scene
tools.description: Instance a .tscn file under a node in the open scene (undoable).

scene_path.description: res:// path of the packed scene

tools.name: open_scene
tools.description: Open a .tscn scene in the editor.

tools.name: create_scene
tools.description: Create a new scene file with a root node and open it.

script_path.description: Optional .gd or .cs script for the root node

tools.name: save_scene
tools.description: Save the currently edited scene, optionally as a new path.

tools.name: get_project_settings
tools.description: Read project settings (ProjectSettings). Filter by key prefix, e.g. application/ or input/.

prefix.description: Only keys starting with this prefix (default "")

tools.name: set_project_setting
tools.description: Set and save one project setting in project.godot.

tools.name: run_project
tools.description: Start play-testing: the main scene, the current scene, or a specific scene.

tools.name: stop_project
tools.description: Stop the running play-test.

tools.name: get_editor_log
tools.description: Read the tail of the Godot editor log. Use after running the game to see runtime errors.

tools.name: scan_filesystem
tools.description: Ask the editor to rescan the project filesystem (needed after writing files outside the plugin, e.g. from git).

tools.name: capture_editor_viewport
tools.description: Save a PNG screenshot of the editor viewport into the project so the human can see it.
